title: The Trenches
desc: World War One — the war that shaped the modern world

questions.q: What event triggered WWI and in which city did it happen?
questions.a: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, 28 June 1914

questions.q: The Christmas Truce of 1914 — what actually happened, and did they really play football?
questions.a: German and British soldiers emerged from trenches, exchanged gifts, sang carols, and yes — informal football matches were played in no man's land. Commanders were furious and ensured it never happened at scale again

questions.q: What was 'shell shock' and what do we call it today?
questions.a: Psychological trauma from sustained combat — now known as PTSD (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder). In WWI many sufferers were accused of cowardice

questions.q: Tanks were first used in which WWI battle, and why were they called 'tanks'?
questions.a: The Battle of the Somme (1916). They were called 'tanks' as a cover story — workers were told they were building mobile water tanks for Mesopotamia

questions.q: How many soldiers died on the first day of the Battle of the Somme alone?
questions.a: About 19,240 British soldiers killed — the bloodiest day in British military history. Total casualties (killed, wounded, missing) were around 57,000

questions.q: The Red Baron was the war's most famous fighter pilot. What was his real name and how many confirmed kills did he have?
questions.a: Manfred von Richthofen — 80 confirmed aerial victories before being shot down in April 1918

questions.q: What was the Gallipoli Campaign and why is it so important to Australia and New Zealand?
questions.a: A failed Allied attempt to capture Constantinople via the Dardanelles (1915-16). The devastating losses at ANZAC Cove became foundational to Australian and New Zealand national identity — ANZAC Day is still commemorated on 25 April

questions.q: Mustard gas was first used in WWI. Why was it called 'mustard' gas?
questions.a: Its smell — described as resembling mustard, garlic, or horseradish. Chemically it's dichlorodiethyl sulfide, a blistering agent that caused horrific burns

questions.q: The war ended at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month — but soldiers were still being ordered to attack that morning. Why?
questions.a: Some commanders wanted to capture final objectives before the ceasefire. Roughly 2,700 soldiers were killed on the last day, including some in the final minutes

questions.q: What did the Treaty of Versailles demand from Germany that many historians believe contributed to WWII?
questions.a: Crippling war reparations (132 billion gold marks), loss of territory, military restrictions, and the 'war guilt clause' — the humiliation and economic devastation fuelled the rise of extremism
